caption:
7 deaths in a single day. 1,753 new hospitalizations. Dengue is surging across Bangladesh.

Seven people died from dengue fever in the last 24 hours, according to a press release from the Health Emergency Operation Center and Control Room of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

During the same period, 1,753 patients were admitted to various hospitals across the country.

The distribution of admissions shows 394 patients in the Dhaka division (outside city corporations), 349 in Khulna, 186 in Barishal, 183 in Mymensingh, 177 in Chittagong, and 153 in Rajshahi.

Within the capital, 175 patients were admitted in Dhaka North City Corporation and 174 in Dhaka South City Corporation.

Other regions reported 53 admissions in Rangpur and 9 in Sylhet.

This brings the total number of deaths from dengue this year to 171, with 56,916 people hospitalized throughout the year.

headline_marked: Dengue claims [[22-year-old student and unborn child]] in Dhaka
headline: Dengue claims 22-year-old student and unborn child in Dhaka
summary: Nur Jahan, a student of Cumilla Victoria Government College, died while undergoing treatment at Bangladesh Medical University.
details: Nur Jahan, a 22-year-old student of the Bangla Department at Cumilla Victoria Government College, died early today at Bangladesh Medical University (BMU) in Dhaka.
According to BMU authorities, Nur Jahan was nine months pregnant, and her unborn child also died during the process.
Her husband, Jobayer Hossain, stated that she developed a mild fever last Friday and later faced complications, leading to her admission to BMU after initial treatment in Cumilla.
Teachers and students of Victoria College expressed deep shock over the loss of the bright student.
Principal Prof Abul Basar Bhuiyan described the death as heartbreaking and offered prayers for the departed soul.
A delegation of college teachers attended her namaz-e-janaza today to express condolences to her family.
caption:
A 22-year-old pregnant student and her unborn child have died of dengue.

Nur Jahan, a 22-year-old student of the Bangla Department at Cumilla Victoria Government College, died early today at Bangladesh Medical University (BMU) in Dhaka.

According to BMU authorities, Nur Jahan was nine months pregnant, and her unborn child also died during the process.

Her husband, Jobayer Hossain, stated that she developed a mild fever last Friday and later faced complications, leading to her admission to BMU after initial treatment in Cumilla.

Teachers and students of Victoria College expressed deep shock over the loss of the bright student.

Principal Prof Abul Basar Bhuiyan described the death as heartbreaking and offered prayers for the departed soul.

A delegation of college teachers attended her namaz-e-janaza today to express condolences to her family.

#Bangladesh #Dengue #HealthCrisis #Cumilla #Dhaka

Source: The Daily Star, Prothom Alo
